sentences.text: Ingentia was a large herbivorous sauropod dinosaur.
Adult specimens are estimated to have reached lengths of 8 to 10 meters and weighed nearly 10 tonnes.
Like other lessemsaurids, it possessed highly pneumatic dorsal and cervical vertebrae, short but tall robust cervical vertebrae, a widely expanded distal scapula blade, and upright arms.
The discovery suggests that gigantism evolved approximately 30 million years earlier than previously thought, before the appearance of the first eusauropods.
The name Ingentia prima was chosen to reference the large body size acquired during the early evolution of dinosaurs.
The fossils were discovered in May 2015 by Diego Abelín and the paleontology team of the UNSJ Institute and Museum of Natural Sciences.
The remains were exhumed from the Balde de Leyes site in the Caucete department, southeast of San Juan province, Argentina.
The type specimen was found in the Quebrada del Barro Formation in northwestern Argentina.
Ingentia was described in 2018 by a team led by Cecilia Apaldetti and colleagues.
Phylogenetic analysis places Ingentia in the family Lessemsauridae, a clade that also includes Lessemsaurus and Antetonitrus.
Ingentia lived during the Late Triassic (late Norian-Rhaetian) in Argentina.
It is debated whether the clade containing Ingentia represents the oldest sauropod taxon or the sister group to Sauropoda, depending on how Sauropoda is defined.
